{ "answer": "The left wing main spar of airplane N104ER experienced a fatigue failure. The SEM images (Figure 20) reveal that the fatigue region is characterized by beach marks and ratchet marks indicative of cyclic loading over time, which are typical signs of fatigue damage. The dashed line in Figure 20 indicates the fatigue boundary, while an unlabeled bracket points to the fatigue origin area where significant material loss has occurred due to fatigue crack initiation (Figure 13). The optical macrograph (Figure 13) shows a polished and etched cross-section with visible beach marks and ratchet marks, further confirming that cyclic loading was responsible for the failure. No clear signs of corrosion or wear are evident in these images; instead, there is evidence of cracks and missing material at the origin area where fatigue crack propagation started.",
